meta.title: The Ghost in the Class Play
meta.textType: story: the gist of an illustrated story

paragraphs: Lily was afraid of the class play, but her friends helped her. Teacher Kim gave her the part of a ghost in a famous old story. Lily had only one line to say. "Who is in my house?" It was a short line, but the stage looked frightening to her. On Wednesday, she took the book home. Lily practiced the line in the living room.

At home, Lily said the line to Pip. Pip took her sock and hid under the sofa. Tom was doing his homework at the table. "Your line is too quiet," he said. "Stand up and say it again, and say it loudly." Lily tried again, and Tom nodded. "Better," said Tom. "But you may forget the line on the stage. Look at one friend, not at all the children."

On Friday, the class sat in the hall. Lily stood behind a blue curtain in a white sheet. Leo was the man in the house. Mia was the helper, and she held the book next to the stage. Lily's hands were cold. Then she looked at Mia and did not see any other face. "Who is in my house?" said Lily. Her line was loud and clear.

Leo jumped back, and the children laughed and clapped. After the play, Mia ran to Lily. "Were you afraid?" she asked. "Actually, I was not afraid at the end," said Lily. Tom and Pip waited at the school gate. Pip had the sock in his mouth again. In the end, the ghost was not frightening for Lily at all.
